request.spec:
A fourth role, restricted, can be assigned. A restricted user sees on the people list only the
people of the crews they lead or belong to (by a person with the user's name) and that person
themselves: no other row is on the screen. Every other figure (the totals row, the header, the
summary, the periods, the pools) is still over everyone on the sheet.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A fourth role, restricted, can be assigned. A restricted user sees on the people list only the
people of the crews they lead or belong to (by a person with the user's name) and that person
themselves: no other row is on the screen. Every other figure (the totals row, the header, the
summary, the periods, the pools) is still over everyone on the sheet.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the restricted role, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What a restricted user sees:** the people list shows only the person whose name matches their user name, plus everyone in the crews that person leads or belongs to. If no person has their name, as with `vic` in the test, they see no rows at all. The totals row, header, summary, periods and pools are still over everyone on the sheet. While the roles and crews are still loading, a restricted user sees no rows rather than briefly seeing everyone.

**Where the filtering happens:** only the rows the people list shows are filtered, in the browser (`features/people/list.slot.tsx`). The server still sends every person, because the totals are worked out from the full list. So this hides rows on the screen; it doesn't stop a restricted user from getting other people's data straight from the API. If it needs to be a real access control, filtering has to move to the server.

**Server changes:**
- `Role` has a new `RESTRICTED` value. Setting the role is audited as `role=restricted`, and the refusal message now lists the fourth role.
- The role column already allowed the new value, so there's no database migration.
- The roles form also offers "restricted" in its suggestions.

**Decisions the request didn't cover:**
- **Permissions:** a restricted user can do whatever a clerk can, including staying within the clerk limit. The request only described visibility, so I didn't restrict actions.
- **Permission settings:** "restricted" can't be listed in a permission setting like `perm-open`, the same as "viewer".
- **Delegations:** the row filter uses the role assigned to the user and ignores delegations. A restricted user who has been delegated the steward role will still only see their own crews' rows.
